source.text: עַ֥ל נַהֲר֨וֹת׀בָּבֶ֗ל שָׁ֣ם יָ֭שַׁבְנוּ גַּם־בָּכִ֑ינוּ בְּ֝זָכְרֵ֗נוּ אֶת־צִיּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: By [the] rivers of Babylon, there we sat, also we wept, when we remembered Zion.

en.L: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat, and we also wept, when we remembered Zion.
en.B: Beside the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down; we wept as we thought of Zion.
en.R: We sat beside the rivers in Babylon, and we cried when we thought about Zion.

fr.L: Près des fleuves de Babylone, là nous nous sommes assis, et nous avons aussi pleuré, en nous souvenant de Sion.
fr.B: Au bord des fleuves de Babylone, là nous nous sommes assis ; nous avons pleuré en pensant à Sion.
fr.R: Nous étions assis près des fleuves, à Babylone, et nous pleurions quand nous pensions à Sion.

sw.L: Karibu na mito ya Babeli, huko tuliketi, nasi pia tulilia, tulipoikumbuka Sayuni.
sw.B: Pembeni mwa mito ya Babeli tuliketi chini; tulilia tukiikumbuka Sayuni.
sw.R: Tuliketi karibu na mito huko Babeli, tukalia tulipofikiria Sayuni.

es.L: Junto a los ríos de Babilonia, allí nos sentamos, y también lloramos, cuando nos acordábamos de Sion.
es.B: A la orilla de los ríos de Babilonia, allí nos sentamos; llorábamos al pensar en Sion.
es.R: Nos sentábamos junto a los ríos de Babilonia, y llorábamos cuando pensábamos en Sion.

vi.L: Bên các dòng sông Ba-by-lôn, tại đó chúng tôi đã ngồi, và chúng tôi cũng đã khóc, khi chúng tôi nhớ đến Si-ôn.
vi.B: Bên bờ các dòng sông Ba-by-lôn, chúng tôi ngồi xuống tại đó; chúng tôi khóc khi nhớ đến Si-ôn.
vi.R: Chúng tôi ngồi bên các dòng sông ở Ba-by-lôn, và chúng tôi khóc khi nghĩ đến Si-ôn.

decisions.choice: by the rivers of Babylon: in exile
decisions.reason: After Jerusalem and its temple were destroyed in 587 or 586 BC, many of its people were taken to Babylon (2 Kings 25:8-11). Babylonia was crossed by the Euphrates and by many canals; Ezekiel lived among the exiles by one of them (Ezekiel 1:1-3). The psalm looks back on that time ("there we sat").

decisions.choice: Zion: Jerusalem, the city of God's temple
decisions.reason: Zion is the hill of the temple and so the city of Jerusalem (verses 5-7), the place where the LORD was worshiped.

decisions.choice: also we wept: we sat and even wept
decisions.reason: The word "also" (gam) adds the weeping to the sitting: they not only sat idle but wept.

decisions.choice: passé composé at Literal and Balanced for the remembered past ("nous nous sommes assis"); imperfect at Readable ("nous étions assis", "nous pleurions")
decisions.reason: The psalm is spoken memory, not written narrative, so French uses the tenses of speech. Readable uses the imperfect for the long time of sitting and weeping, which also keeps it clear of the familiar wording of older French versions.

decisions.choice: "Ba-by-lôn" for Babylon
decisions.reason: The name takes the Protestant tradition's form, which Vietnamese Bible readers know.

records.literal_gloss: On [the] poplars in its midst we hung up our lyres.

en.L: On the poplars in its midst we hung up our lyres.
en.B: On the poplar trees there we hung up our lyres.
en.R: We hung our harps on the poplar trees there.

fr.L: Aux peupliers au milieu d’elle, nous avons suspendu nos lyres.
fr.B: Aux peupliers de ce pays, nous avons suspendu nos lyres.
fr.R: Nous avions accroché nos harpes aux peupliers de là-bas.

sw.L: Juu ya mipopla katikati yake tulivitundika vinubi vyetu.
sw.B: Juu ya miti ya mipopla huko tulivitundika vinubi vyetu.
sw.R: Tulivitundika vinubi vyetu kwenye miti ya mipopla huko.

es.L: En los álamos que hay en medio de ella colgamos nuestras liras.
es.B: En los álamos de aquel lugar colgamos nuestras liras.
es.R: Colgamos nuestras arpas en los álamos de allí.

vi.L: Trên những cây dương ở giữa nó, chúng tôi đã treo những đàn lia của chúng tôi.
vi.B: Chúng tôi treo đàn lia của mình trên những cây dương ở đó.
vi.R: Chúng tôi treo những cây đàn hạc của mình trên những cây dương ở đó.

decisions.choice: poplars: trees that grow by water
decisions.reason: The tree ('aravah) grows beside streams (Isaiah 44:4). It is probably the poplar of the Euphrates; older translations say "willows".

decisions.choice: we hung up our lyres: no songs in exile
decisions.reason: The lyre (kinnor) went with songs of joy and praise (33:2). Hanging it up means the music has stopped (Isaiah 24:8).

decisions.choice: in its midst: in Babylon
decisions.reason: "Its" is Babylon, or its land.

decisions.choice: harps
decisions.reason: Readable uses the more familiar name for a stringed instrument, as in 43:4.

decisions.choice: "mipopla" (poplar trees) and "vinubi" (lyres, harps)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew tree is most likely the Euphrates poplar, so Swahili names the poplar, as the English does, rather than the willow of older translations. "Kinubi" is the Swahili word for a stringed instrument plucked by hand, covering both the English "lyre" and "harp".

decisions.choice: "đàn lia" (L, B); "đàn hạc" (R)
decisions.reason: The instrument is a small hand-held stringed lyre; "đàn lia" names it, and Readable says "đàn hạc" (harp), the more familiar word, as the English Readable says "harps".

source.text: כִּ֤י שָׁ֨ם שְֽׁאֵל֪וּנוּ שׁוֹבֵ֡ינוּ דִּבְרֵי־שִׁ֭יר וְתוֹלָלֵ֣ינוּ שִׂמְחָ֑ה שִׁ֥ירוּ לָ֝֗נוּ מִשִּׁ֥יר צִיּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: For there our captors asked us [for] words of a song, and our tormentors [for] joy: Sing for us from [the] song[s] of Zion!

en.L: For there our captors asked us for words of song, and our tormentors [asked for] joy: "Sing for us [one] of the songs of Zion!"
en.B: For there the people who had taken us captive demanded songs from us; those who tormented us wanted us to be cheerful: "Sing for us a song from Zion!"
en.R: There the people who had captured us wanted us to sing. They mocked us and wanted us to sing happy songs. They said, "Sing us a song from Zion!"

fr.L: Car là nos ravisseurs nous ont demandé des paroles de chant, et nos tourmenteurs de la joie : « Chantez-nous [un] des chants de Sion ! »
fr.B: Car là, ceux qui nous avaient emmenés captifs exigeaient de nous des chants ; ceux qui nous tourmentaient voulaient de la gaieté : « Chantez-nous un chant de Sion ! »
fr.R: Là-bas, les gens qui nous avaient faits prisonniers voulaient que nous chantions. Ils se moquaient de nous et voulaient des chants joyeux. Ils disaient : « Chantez-nous un chant de Sion ! »

sw.L: Kwa maana huko waliotuteka walituomba maneno ya wimbo, na watesi wetu [waliomba] furaha: "Tuimbieni [mmoja] wa nyimbo za Sayuni!"
sw.B: Kwa maana huko watu waliotuchukua mateka walitutaka tuwaimbie; wale waliotutesa walitaka tuwe na furaha: "Tuimbieni wimbo wa Sayuni!"
sw.R: Huko watu waliotuteka walitaka tuimbe. Walitudhihaki na kutaka tuimbe nyimbo za furaha. Walisema, "Tuimbieni wimbo wa Sayuni!"

es.L: Porque allí nuestros captores nos pedían palabras de canto, y nuestros atormentadores [nos pedían] alegría: «¡{{plural_you:Cántennos|Cantadnos}} [uno] de los cánticos de Sion!».
es.B: Porque allí los que nos habían llevado cautivos nos exigían canciones; los que nos atormentaban querían que estuviéramos alegres: «¡{{plural_you:Cántennos|Cantadnos}} un canto de Sion!».
es.R: Allí la gente que nos había capturado quería que cantáramos. Se burlaban de nosotros y querían que cantáramos canciones alegres. Decían: «¡{{plural_you:Cántennos|Cantadnos}} un canto de Sion!».

vi.L: Vì tại đó những kẻ bắt chúng tôi làm phu tù đòi chúng tôi những lời ca, và những kẻ hành hạ chúng tôi [đòi] niềm vui: "Hãy hát cho chúng ta nghe [một] trong những bài ca của Si-ôn!"
vi.B: Vì tại đó những kẻ đã bắt chúng tôi làm phu tù đòi chúng tôi hát; những kẻ hành hạ chúng tôi muốn chúng tôi vui vẻ: "Hãy hát cho chúng ta nghe một bài ca của Si-ôn!"
vi.R: Ở đó, những kẻ đã bắt chúng tôi muốn chúng tôi hát. Chúng chế nhạo chúng tôi và muốn chúng tôi hát những bài ca vui vẻ. Chúng nói: "Hãy hát cho chúng ta một bài ca của Si-ôn đi!"

decisions.choice: our tormentors: those who mocked us
decisions.reason: This word (tolal) is found only here. It is usually linked with a verb for mocking or with a word for plunder; the ancient Greek translation reads "those who led us away".

decisions.choice: the songs of Zion: songs of the temple
decisions.reason: Songs sung at the temple in Jerusalem, such as Psalms 46, 48 and 87, which praise Zion as the city God will never let fall. To ask for them among the ruins was mockery.

decisions.choice: joy: songs of joy
decisions.reason: Joy (simchah) here is the cheerful music of a feast, demanded of people in grief.

decisions.choice: They mocked us
decisions.reason: Readable turns the noun into a sentence (m1).

decisions.choice: plural_you on "Cántennos"
decisions.reason: The captors' command "sing for us" is plural, spoken to the exiles; Spanish marks it with the plural_you setting.

source.text: אֵ֗יךְ נָשִׁ֥יר אֶת־שִׁיר־יְהוָ֑ה עַ֝֗ל אַדְמַ֥ת נֵכָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: How will we sing the song of YHWH on [the] ground of foreignness?

en.L: How shall we sing the song of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on foreign ground?
en.B: How could we sing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s song in a land of strangers?
en.R: But how could we sing the songs of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} while we were living in a foreign country?

fr.L: Comment chanterions-nous le chant {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} sur une terre étrangère ?
fr.B: Comment pourrions-nous chanter le chant {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} dans un pays d’étrangers ?
fr.R: Mais comment aurions-nous pu chanter les chants {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} alors que nous vivions dans un pays étranger ?

sw.L: Tutauimbaje wimbo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} katika ardhi ya kigeni?
sw.B: Tungewezaje kuuimba wimbo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} katika nchi ya wageni?
sw.R: Lakini tungewezaje kuimba nyimbo za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} tukiwa tunaishi katika nchi ya kigeni?

es.L: ¿Cómo cantaremos el cántico {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} en tierra extranjera?
es.B: ¿Cómo podríamos cantar el cántico {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} en una tierra de extraños?
es.R: Pero ¿cómo podíamos cantar los cantos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} mientras vivíamos en un país extranjero?

vi.L: Làm sao chúng tôi hát bài ca của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trên đất ngoại bang?
vi.B: Làm sao chúng tôi có thể hát bài ca của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nơi xứ lạ quê người?
vi.R: Nhưng làm sao chúng tôi có thể hát những bài ca của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} khi đang sống nơi đất khách?

decisions.choice: the song of the LORD: a song of his worship
decisions.reason: The songs of Zion (verse 3) are the LORD's own songs, sung in his house. To sing them for the amusement of their captors, in a land of other gods, was unthinkable (compare Amos 7:17).

decisions.choice: How shall we sing: a refusal
decisions.reason: The question is an answer to the captors: it cannot be done.

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: Readable marks the question as the answer to the demand of verse 3 (m2).

records.literal_gloss: If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right [hand] forget.

en.L: If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right [hand] forget.
en.B: Jerusalem, if I ever forget you, may my right hand forget how to play.
en.R: Jerusalem, if I ever forget you, may my right hand never play the harp again.

fr.L: Si je t’oublie, Jérusalem, que ma droite oublie !
fr.B: Jérusalem, si jamais je t’oublie, que ma main droite oublie comment jouer !
fr.R: Jérusalem, si jamais je t’oublie, que ma main droite ne joue plus jamais de la harpe !

sw.L: Kama nitakusahau, Yerusalemu, [mkono] wangu wa kuume na usahau.
sw.B: Yerusalemu, nikiwahi kukusahau, mkono wangu wa kulia na usahau jinsi ya kupiga kinubi.
sw.R: Yerusalemu, nikiwahi kukusahau, mkono wangu wa kulia na usipige kinubi tena kamwe.

es.L: Si me olvido de ti, Jerusalén, que mi [mano] derecha olvide.
es.B: Jerusalén, si alguna vez me olvido de ti, que mi mano derecha olvide cómo tocar.
es.R: Jerusalén, si alguna vez me olvido de ti, que mi mano derecha nunca vuelva a tocar el arpa.

vi.L: Hỡi Giê-ru-sa-lem, nếu tôi quên ngươi, nguyện tay phải tôi quên [tài khéo của nó].
vi.B: Hỡi Giê-ru-sa-lem, nếu tôi quên ngươi, nguyện tay phải tôi quên cách gảy đàn.
vi.R: Giê-ru-sa-lem ơi, nếu tôi quên thành, nguyện tay phải tôi không bao giờ còn gảy đàn được nữa.

decisions.choice: If I forget you: one singer's oath
decisions.reason: The "we" of verses 1-4 becomes "I", and the singer speaks to Jerusalem. Verses 5-6 are an oath that calls a penalty on oneself.

decisions.choice: may my right hand forget: lose its skill
decisions.reason: The verb has no object: the hand that plays the lyre is to "forget" its skill, a play on "if I forget you". A small change of letters would give "wither".

decisions.choice: how to play (B); never play the harp again (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the hand would forget (m2).

decisions.choice: "tôi" for the singer and "ngươi" (L, B) for Jerusalem, as in Psalm 122
decisions.reason: One singer makes an oath to the city (see the meaning decision). As in Psalm 122, the city is spoken to as "ngươi" at Literal and Balanced and by name at Readable.

source.text: תִּדְבַּ֥ק־לְשׁוֹנִ֨י׀לְחִכִּי֮ אִם־לֹ֪א אֶ֫זְכְּרֵ֥כִי אִם־לֹ֣א אַ֭עֲלֶה אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֑ם עַ֝֗ל רֹ֣אשׁ שִׂמְחָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: May my tongue cling to my palate if not I remember you, if not I lift up Jerusalem above [the] head of my joy.

en.L: May my tongue cling to my palate if I do not remember you, if I do not lift up Jerusalem above the head of my joy.
en.B: May my tongue stay stuck to the roof of my mouth should I fail to remember you, should I fail to prize Jerusalem above my chief delight.
en.R: May my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth and never sing again if I do not remember you, if Jerusalem is not my greatest joy.

fr.L: Que ma langue s’attache à mon palais si je ne me souviens pas de toi, si je n’élève pas Jérusalem au-dessus du sommet de ma joie !
fr.B: Que ma langue reste collée à mon palais si je manque à me souvenir de toi, si je ne mets pas Jérusalem au-dessus de ma plus grande joie !
fr.R: Que ma langue reste collée à mon palais et ne chante plus jamais si je ne me souviens pas de toi, si Jérusalem n’est pas ma plus grande joie !

sw.L: Ulimi wangu na ushikamane na kaakaa langu nisipokukumbuka, nisipouinua Yerusalemu juu ya kichwa cha furaha yangu.
sw.B: Ulimi wangu na ubaki umegandamana na kaakaa langu nikishindwa kukukumbuka, nikishindwa kuuthamini Yerusalemu kuliko furaha yangu kuu.
sw.R: Ulimi wangu na ushikamane na kaakaa la kinywa changu nisiimbe tena kamwe, kama sitakukumbuka, kama Yerusalemu si furaha yangu kubwa kuliko zote.

es.L: Que se pegue mi lengua a mi paladar si no me acuerdo de ti, si no pongo a Jerusalén por encima de la cumbre de mi alegría.
es.B: Que mi lengua se quede pegada al paladar si dejo de acordarme de ti, si no aprecio a Jerusalén por encima de mi mayor alegría.
es.R: Que mi lengua se pegue al paladar y nunca vuelva a cantar si no me acuerdo de ti, si Jerusalén no es mi mayor alegría.

vi.L: Nguyện lưỡi tôi dính vào vòm miệng tôi, nếu tôi không nhớ đến ngươi, nếu tôi không đặt Giê-ru-sa-lem lên trên niềm vui cao nhất của tôi.
vi.B: Nguyện lưỡi tôi dính chặt vào vòm miệng, nếu tôi không còn nhớ đến ngươi, nếu tôi không quý Giê-ru-sa-lem hơn cả niềm vui lớn nhất của tôi.
vi.R: Nguyện lưỡi tôi dính vào vòm miệng và không bao giờ còn hát được nữa, nếu tôi không nhớ đến thành, nếu Giê-ru-sa-lem không phải là niềm vui lớn nhất của tôi.

decisions.choice: may my tongue cling to my palate: may I never sing again
decisions.reason: A tongue stuck to the roof of the mouth cannot speak or sing (Ezekiel 3:26). The penalty matches the hand of verse 5: no more playing, no more singing.

decisions.choice: the head of my joy: my highest joy
decisions.reason: "Head" is the top or chief: Jerusalem must rank above every other joy.

decisions.choice: and never sing again
decisions.reason: Readable says what the penalty means (m1).

source.text: זְכֹ֤ר יְהוָ֨ה׀לִבְנֵ֬י אֱד֗וֹם אֵת֮ י֤וֹם יְֽרוּשָׁ֫לִָ֥ם הָ֭אֹ֣מְרִים עָ֤רוּ׀עָ֑רוּ עַ֝֗ד הַיְס֥וֹד בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Remember, YHWH, against [the] sons of Edom the day of Jerusalem, those saying: Lay [it] bare, lay [it] bare to the foundation in it!

en.L: Remember, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, against the sons of Edom the day of Jerusalem, who said, "Lay [it] bare, lay [it] bare to the foundation in it!"
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, hold the day of Jerusalem's fall against the Edomites, who shouted, "Strip it, strip it bare, right down to its foundations!"
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, remember what the people of Edom did on the day Jerusalem was destroyed. They shouted, "Wreck it! Wreck it right down to its foundations!"

fr.L: Souviens-toi, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, contre les fils d’Édom, du jour de Jérusalem, de ceux qui disaient : « Rasez, rasez jusqu’aux fondations en elle ! »
fr.B: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, tiens compte contre les Édomites du jour où Jérusalem est tombée, eux qui criaient : « Rasez-la, rasez-la jusqu’à ses fondations ! »
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, souviens-toi de ce qu’ont fait les gens d’Édom le jour où Jérusalem a été détruite. Ils criaient : « Démolissez-la ! Démolissez-la jusqu’à ses fondations ! »

sw.L: Kumbuka, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, juu ya wana wa Edomu siku ya Yerusalemu, waliosema, "Ufunueni, ufunueni mpaka msingi wake!"
sw.B: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, uwahesabie Waedomu siku ile ya kuanguka kwa Yerusalemu, waliopiga kelele, "Uvueni, uvueni kabisa, mpaka misingi yake!"
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ukumbuke yale ambayo watu wa Edomu walifanya siku Yerusalemu ulipoharibiwa. Walipiga kelele, "Ubomoeni! Ubomoeni mpaka misingi yake!"

es.L: Acuérdate, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, contra los hijos de Edom del día de Jerusalén, los que decían: «¡{{plural_you:Arrásenla|Arrasadla}}, {{plural_you:arrásenla|arrasadla}} hasta los cimientos!».
es.B: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, toma en cuenta contra los edomitas el día de la caída de Jerusalén, cuando gritaban: «¡{{plural_you:Desnúdenla|Desnudadla}}, {{plural_you:déjenla|dejadla}} pelada hasta los cimientos!».
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, acuérdate de lo que hizo la gente de Edom el día en que Jerusalén fue destruida. Gritaban: «¡{{plural_you:Destrúyanla|Destruidla}}! ¡{{plural_you:Destrúyanla|Destruidla}} hasta los cimientos!».

vi.L: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin nhớ lại ngày của Giê-ru-sa-lem mà buộc tội con cái Ê-đôm, là những kẻ đã nói: "Hãy san bằng, hãy san bằng nó đến tận nền móng!"
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin nhớ mà buộc tội người Ê-đôm về ngày Giê-ru-sa-lem thất thủ, là những kẻ đã la lên: "Hãy phá đi, hãy phá sạch đến tận nền móng!"
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin nhớ lại điều dân Ê-đôm đã làm vào ngày Giê-ru-sa-lem bị tàn phá. Chúng đã la lên: "Phá đi! Phá sập nó đến tận nền móng!"

decisions.choice: the sons of Edom: Judah's neighbors and kin
decisions.reason: Edom, the people descended from Esau, Jacob's brother, lived south-east of Judah. When Babylon took Jerusalem, Edom cheered and joined in the plunder (Obadiah 10-14; Lamentations 4:21-22; Ezekiel 25:12).

decisions.choice: the day of Jerusalem: the day the city fell
decisions.reason: "The day" of a city or people is the day of its disaster (Obadiah 12).

decisions.choice: lay bare: tear down to nothing
decisions.reason: The verb ('arah) is to strip or empty out; of a city, to tear down its walls and houses to the foundations.

decisions.choice: remember against: hold it against them
decisions.reason: To remember something against someone is to bring it into judgment (Nehemiah 13:29).

decisions.choice: the Edomites (B); the people of Edom (R)
decisions.reason: "Sons of" a nation are its people (m1).

decisions.choice: "les fils d'Édom" at Literal, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: "Sons of Edom" names the people of Edom, as Balanced and Readable say; the English has no setting either, so French keeps the Hebrew phrase at Literal as it stands.

decisions.choice: the Edomites' shout as a plural command (Arrásenla, Desnúdenla, Destrúyanla)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "lay it bare" is a plural command, the Edomites urging on the attackers. Spanish marks the forms with the plural_you setting.

decisions.choice: "con cái Ê-đôm" (L); "người Ê-đôm" (B); "dân Ê-đôm" (R)
decisions.reason: "Sons of Edom" means the people of Edom (see the meaning decision); Literal keeps the family word with "con cái", and the other levels say the people, as the English does.

source.text: בַּת־בָּבֶ֗ל הַשְּׁד֫וּדָ֥ה אַשְׁרֵ֥י שֶׁיְשַׁלֶּם־לָ֑ךְ אֶת־גְּ֝מוּלֵ֗ךְ שֶׁגָּמַ֥לְתְּ לָֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Daughter of Babylon, the devastated, how blessed [is the one] who repays to you your dealing that you dealt to us!

en.L: Daughter of Babylon, [you who are to be] devastated, how blessed [is the one] who repays you the deed that you did to us!
en.B: Daughter Babylon, soon to be laid waste, how blessed is the one who pays you back in full for all you did to us!
en.R: People of Babylon, you will soon be destroyed. Happy is the one who pays you back for what you did to us!

fr.L: Fille de Babylone, [toi qui seras] dévastée, heureux [celui] qui te rendra ce que tu nous as fait !
fr.B: Fille de Babylone, bientôt dévastée, heureux celui qui te rendra pleinement tout ce que tu nous as fait !
fr.R: Peuple de Babylone, tu seras bientôt détruit. Heureux celui qui te fera payer ce que tu nous as fait !

sw.L: Ee binti Babeli, [wewe utakayeangamizwa], heri [yule] atakayekulipa kwa tendo ulilotutendea!
sw.B: Ee binti Babeli, utakayeharibiwa hivi karibuni, heri yule atakayekulipa kikamilifu kwa yote uliyotutendea!
sw.R: Watu wa Babeli, mtaangamizwa hivi karibuni. Atakuwa na furaha yule atakayewalipa kwa yale mliyotutendea!

es.L: Hija de Babilonia, [la que será] devastada, ¡dichoso [el] que te devuelva el pago que tú nos hiciste!
es.B: Hija de Babilonia, que pronto serás asolada, ¡qué dichoso el que te pague con creces todo lo que nos hiciste!
es.R: Pueblo de Babilonia, pronto serás destruido. ¡Feliz el que te pague por lo que nos hiciste!

vi.L: Hỡi con gái Ba-by-lôn, [kẻ sẽ bị] tàn phá, phước thay [người] báo trả cho ngươi việc ngươi đã làm cho chúng tôi!
vi.B: Hỡi con gái Ba-by-lôn, kẻ sắp bị tàn phá, phước hạnh thay người báo trả ngươi cho đủ mọi điều ngươi đã làm cho chúng tôi!
vi.R: Hỡi dân Ba-by-lôn, các ngươi sắp bị tiêu diệt. Thật hạnh phúc cho người nào báo trả các ngươi về những gì các ngươi đã làm cho chúng tôi!

decisions.choice: daughter of Babylon: the city and its people
decisions.reason: A city is often pictured as a woman, its "daughter" being the city and its people (Isaiah 47:1; Jeremiah 50:42).

decisions.choice: the devastated: Babylon whose ruin is sure
decisions.reason: The word is passive, "devastated". It speaks of Babylon's ruin as already settled, as the prophets announced it (Isaiah 47; Jeremiah 50-51). With one vowel changed it would read "you destroyer".

decisions.choice: repay you what you did to us
decisions.reason: Jeremiah says the same of Babylon: "repay her for her deeds; do to her as she has done" (Jeremiah 50:15, 29; 51:24).

decisions.choice: how blessed: how fortunate
decisions.reason: The word ('ashre) is the one that opens Psalm 1. Here it says how fortunate the one will be who carries out the judgment on Babylon.

decisions.choice: Happy is
decisions.reason: Readable usually says "Life is truly good for" (1:1), but this blessing is on the one who will bring Babylon's judgment, so Readable says "Happy is".

decisions.choice: "Atakuwa na furaha yule" (that one will be glad) at Readable, for "how blessed"
alternatives: "Maisha ni mazuri kweli kwa", as in Psalm 127:5
decisions.reason: Here the English Readable says "Happy is" rather than "Life is truly good for"; Swahili Readable follows it, so that the line is a cry about the one who brings justice and not a description of a good life.

decisions.choice: Feliz (R)
alternatives: Qué buena es la vida de
decisions.reason: Here the English Readable says "Happy is" rather than its usual wording for ashre, since the line is about the one who will carry out the judgment. Spanish Readable follows it with "Feliz"; Literal and Balanced keep "dichoso".

decisions.choice: "con gái Ba-by-lôn" (L, B); "dân Ba-by-lôn" (R); "phước thay" (L), "phước hạnh thay" (B), "Thật hạnh phúc cho" (R) as Psalm 1:1
decisions.reason: "Daughter of Babylon" is the city and its people (see the meaning decision); Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew picture, Readable says who is meant. The exclamation keeps the wording of Psalm 1:1.

records.literal_gloss: How blessed [is the one] who seizes and dashes your little ones against the rock!

en.L: How blessed [is the one] who seizes and dashes your little ones against the rock!
en.B: How blessed is the one who grabs your little children and smashes them on the rock!
en.R: Happy is the one who grabs your babies and smashes them against the rocks!

fr.L: Heureux [celui] qui saisira et écrasera tes petits contre le rocher !
fr.B: Heureux celui qui saisira tes petits enfants et les fracassera contre le rocher !
fr.R: Heureux celui qui attrapera tes bébés et les écrasera contre les rochers !

sw.L: Heri [yule] atakayewakamata watoto wako wachanga na kuwaponda juu ya mwamba!
sw.B: Heri yule atakayewanyakua watoto wako wadogo na kuwapiga juu ya mwamba!
sw.R: Atakuwa na furaha yule atakayewanyakua watoto wenu wachanga na kuwapiga kwenye miamba!

es.L: ¡Dichoso [el] que agarre y estrelle a tus pequeños contra la roca!
es.B: ¡Qué dichoso el que agarre a tus niños pequeños y los estrelle contra la roca!
es.R: ¡Feliz el que agarre a tus bebés y los estrelle contra las rocas!

vi.L: Phước thay [người] bắt lấy và đập con nhỏ của ngươi vào đá!
vi.B: Phước hạnh thay người túm lấy những đứa con nhỏ của ngươi mà đập chúng vào đá!
vi.R: Thật hạnh phúc cho người nào túm lấy con nhỏ của các ngươi và đập chúng vào đá!

decisions.choice: a cry for judgment on Babylon
decisions.reason: The psalm ends with the grief and anger of people who saw their city destroyed and their own children die (Lamentations 2:20-21; 4:10). They ask that Babylon suffer what it did, the judgment the prophets announced against it (Isaiah 13:16). They do not take revenge themselves but leave it with God (verse 7; Deuteronomy 32:35; Romans 12:19). The words are not softened: they are part of Scripture's honest prayer.

decisions.choice: your little ones: young children
decisions.reason: The word ('olel) is a young child, still small enough to be carried.

decisions.choice: dashed against the rock: a horror of ancient war
decisions.reason: Conquering armies killed children in this way, and the prophets name it among the horrors of a city's fall (Isaiah 13:16).

decisions.choice: Happy is
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.
